llm.summary: This healthcare reconciliation skill advertises local use but its entry script is designed to send pasted healthcare tables and persistent identifiers to a remote service, so it needs user review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Remote submission of potentially sensitive medical and financial table data, plus install and subscription identifiers, is high-impact and under-disclosed for a skill described as local and requiring no API key.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate installer or dependency install script was found. Runtime use is via Bash/Node, with --input reading user-selected files and payment/subscription activation handled by the runner.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md invites users to paste healthcare, billing, insurance, and pharmacy tables and says the skill runs locally, while scripts/run.mjs posts that text to a remote endpoint before optionally running bundled engines locally.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The runner creates ~/.healthcare-expert, stores a persistent install-id, subscription/license tokens, and 402 bill files. No background service, privilege escalation, or destructive persistence was found, but the persistent state is not clearly disclosed in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The package coherently contains eight healthcare/pharmacy reconciliation engines matching the listed subskills, but the main runner does not provide fully local routing as advertised; it relies on a remote expert endpoint and currently fails at startup because BASE is undefined.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with pasted healthcare, billing, insurance, and pharmacy tables being sent to the publisher-operated service and with a hidden local folder storing install/payment state. Redact patient identifiers and other PHI/PII first. Also note that the provided runner currently fails because BASE is undefined, so the advertised workflow may not work as packaged.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The scanner treated individual engine files as scope mismatches, but the total package includes all eight listed engines; the remaining mismatch is that local auto-routing is not implemented in the visible runner without the remote service.
[SDI-1] expected: Medical-device traceability and insurance-denial modules are present in SKILL.md and the manifest, so those modules are not unexpected; the concern is documentation and runtime clarity, not hidden unrelated capability.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in part: scripts/run.mjs calls itself a thin client with no bundled rule implementation, but the package includes local engines and conditionally executes them after remote authorization.
[LP1] unexpected: Accepted in substance for scripts/run.mjs: it uses fetch to send user text, install id, and subscription/license headers to remote endpoints while SKILL.md advertises local execution. The separate env-capability claim against the cold-chain engine was not supported by inspected code.
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: scripts/run.mjs was locally available and inspected; it is not evidence of analysis evasion in this review.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: the skill targets healthcare and payment/insurance tables but does not prominently instruct users to redact PHI/PII before pasting data, despite remote submission in the runner.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only interface is consistent with the Chinese skill name, examples, and healthcare workflow framing; this is a usability/locale limitation rather than a security concern.
[aig-skill-scan] expected: The supplied SARIF run reported no T01-T09 results; this did not override the artifact-backed concerns above.
